messages:
maya: Quick announcement: we're enabling release annotations in the SDK CI and auto-generating changelogs + migration notes. Aim is clearer release notes and fewer back-and-forths with support. Read the plan: https://redwood.internal/docs/release-annotations
ben: Nice. What do annotations look like? Who adds them?
maya: Annotations are small YAML blocks in PR bodies (see template). Maintainers or authors add them when the change affects public surface, defaults, or behavior. CI will parse them and include them in the changelog.
lucy: Example PR annotation?
maya: ```
release-annotation: |
  impact: minor
  area: sdk-js
  changes:
    - type: param_rename
      from: oldTimeout
      to: requestTimeout
      migration_snippet: ./migrations/oldTimeout-to-requestTimeout.js
```
ben: Does CI validate the annotation schema? We should avoid typos.
ci-bot: CI check redwood/release-annotations will validate schema and ensure required fields for impact >= minor. See: docs/ci/annotation-schema.md
lucy: How do we get the migration snippet into the auto-changelog?
maya: CI will upload snippets as artifacts and a generated markdown section will be embedded into the release notes with code tabs for JS/Python. Docs pipeline will also create a "migration gist" we can link in the dashboard.
release-bot: Canary run: release-annotations-canary scheduled 2025-06-01T12:00Z. Will include annotation parsing, snippet upload, and changelog generation.
ben: Legal/regulatory concern: any new code samples that show PII-like data require review. How do we gate samples?
maya: Good catch. New samples with potential sensitive data must include a `sensitive: true` flag in the annotation. That triggers legal-bot review before snippet is published.
legal-bot: When sensitive=true, please attach a brief justification and a sanitized example in PR. Legal review SLA: 72h.
lucy: What about existing releases? Can we retro-populate annotations for past PRs?
maya: We can run a migration job that scans merged PRs and creates draft annotations where detectable (renames, exported symbol changes). It'll be best-effort and flagged for maintainer review.
ben: How will customers see these changelogs? Console, email, or changelog page?
maya: All three. Primary: release notes page with per-release migration section, an in-console "What's Changed" drawer for active API keys, and an email digest for subscribers. Enterprise CSMs get a CSV of affected customers when impact >= major.
ci-bot: Note: PRs without annotations that touch public API will now get a docs-lint warning. Blocker only for impact >= major.
lucy: Can we automate snippet generation for simple renames? I can add a codemod that creates a suggested snippet automatically and attaches it to the PR as a comment.
maya: Please do. That will reduce friction. Make sure codemod output is reviewed before publishing.
ben: Rollout plan? We need a short transition window so maintainers can adopt annotations.
maya: Rollout: week 1 - enable CI validation + warning; week 2 - auto-changelog in canary; week 3 - enforce blocker for major. We'll publish a migration guide and a short video for maintainers.
legal-bot: FYI: samples with third-party copyright code must include attribution. Add `attribution` key in annotation for those cases.
lucy: One more: how will this interact with SDK internal builds (dedicated/private)? We shouldn't leak internal-only notes.
maya: The CI will mark notes as public/private based on the PR labels. Private notes only appear in enterprise dashboards and internal changelog artifacts. Authors must set `visibility: private` when applicable.
ben: Sounds good. I'll update the PR template and add a lint rule to suggest an annotation when public surface is touched.
maya: Thanks — tagging @release and @docs for follow-up. I'll post the template and a short FAQ in #devex after the canary run. :memo:
